claims.claim: Meta's current causal chain is advertising monetization -> operating cash generation -> AI/data-center infrastructure investment -> model/recommendation capability -> engagement and advertiser performance; Q2 2026 evidence supports the monetization and investment links but does not yet prove the incremental return on the newest AI capex.

factors.name: AI infrastructure causal conversion
factors.basis: Revenue, ad impressions and ad pricing grew strongly while capex accelerated sharply; the bridge from infrastructure spend to durable incremental monetization remains the key falsifiable link.

factors.name: scenario robustness
factors.basis: Large cash generation and scaled ad demand support resilience, while unusually high infrastructure intensity creates a successor bottleneck in power, compute deployment and return-on-capital conversion.

risks.risk: If incremental AI infrastructure fails to sustain engagement, ad efficiency or new monetization at adequate returns, the current positive causal chain weakens despite strong top-line growth.

causalEdges.evidence: Q2 revenue and ad metrics grew double digits alongside substantial operating cash flow.
Current results establish investment intensity and strong monetization concurrently, not the incremental causal return of newest spend.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental return on the newest AI/data-center capex is not separable from current quarter disclosures.

claims.claim: The strongest present challenge is not demand collapse but capital-conversion risk: Q2 costs and expenses rose 55% year over year and capex reached $31.08B while free cash flow was only $784M despite $31.86B operating cash flow.

factors.name: capital intensity and conversion risk
factors.basis: Rapid infrastructure spending materially compresses near-term free-cash conversion even as core advertising execution remains strong.

risks.risk: High fixed infrastructure commitments raise downside sensitivity if AI monetization or engagement benefits arrive slower than spending growth.
Legal charges and severance can obscure normalized cost trends, increasing interpretation uncertainty.

causalEdges.evidence: Q2 operating cash flow of $31.86B translated to $784M free cash flow amid $31.08B capex.

contradictions.claimA: Core advertising demand and pricing are strong.
contradictions.claimB: Near-term free-cash conversion is weak because infrastructure spending is exceptionally high.
contradictions.resolution: These are simultaneous operating facts rather than mutually exclusive claims; the unresolved economic question is future return on the investment, treated as a non-gating unknown rather than a fabricated contradiction.

unknowns.unknown: Current evidence does not quantify the portion of AI capex that is maintenance versus growth or its eventual project-level return.
